title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - roles, stop/logprobs, streaming tool/function-calls, response formatting
author: Alex Morgan
description:
Summary: Implements parity for OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface focusing on: 1) roles and message format compatibility, 2) stop sequences and streaming logprobs emission, 3) streaming stability and retry behavior for tool/function calling, and 4) response formatting (content/choices structure + function_call object). Motivation: downstream customers expect drop-in compatibility for popular OpenAI SDKs and test harnesses; parity reduces friction in migrations and cross-provider comparison. Changes include API layer mappings, streaming protocol improvements, and tests/docs.

What changed (high level):
- Add support for roles parameter mapping (system/user/assistant) and history canonicalization in the OpenAI compatibility layer so incoming messages map to the internal conversation model with preserved metadata.
- Support "stop" sequences in both non-streaming and streaming paths; when streaming, tokens that trigger stops emit final events and stop the stream gracefully.
- Emit streaming "logprobs" packets in a backwards-compatible envelope; enable optional logprobs-on-stream for debug use.
- Implement function/tool-calling parity: when model triggers a tool call, we emit a structured function_call object in the final choice and stream intermediate tool-arguments in an idempotent way to survive reconnects.
- Streaming stability: improved resume semantics and idempotent event sequence numbers, tightened timeouts and retriable checkpoints to avoid duplicate tool invocations on client reconnects.
- Response formatting: choices align with OpenAI shape (index, message/role/content, finish_reason) and function_call sub-object; we added deterministic ordering and truncated token-affecting metadata to maintain parity.
- Tests and docs: extensive integration tests against the parity harness, unit tests for stop/logprobs/roles, and a new compat doc with examples and migration notes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Roles mapping and request validation
- [x] Stops support in streaming and non-streaming
- [x] Streaming logprobs envelope (opt-in)
- [x] Function/tool call streaming and final function_call object
- [x] Resume/reconnect behavior and idempotency checks
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Docs and examples updated

Backward compatibility notes: existing Redwood API callers are unaffected by default; OpenAI-compat is opt-in on routes that enable the compat layer. Function-calling semantics are additive. The streaming logprobs feature is opt-in to avoid bandwidth changes for customers who do not need it.

Performance/behavior: we ran perf canaries and saw no meaningful latency regressions for default workloads; enabling logprobs adds token bandwidth. A small set of benchmarks were included in the PR description and CI is running nightly perf jobs to validate throughput on Dedicated.

Linear references: ENG-3421 (compat parity), PM-1284 (product reqs).

review_comments: Priya Patel commented: Can you clarify how role renaming is handled when clients pass a deprecated role field? Please add a unit test for wrong role values.
Author (Alex Morgan) replied: We canonicalize unknown role tokens to 'user' and log a metrics counter; added unit tests in test_role_mapping.rs and a note in the docs.

Johan Svensson commented: Streaming reconnect/resume looks good but we need stronger invariants to avoid double tool invocation. Suggest sequence-numbered checkpoints and idempotency token.
Action: added idempotency token and deterministic resume logic.

Liang Chen commented: minor nits in the docs and a request to avoid exposing raw logits by default.
Author replied: logprobs are opt-in via the 'logprobs' query param; updated docs and examples accordingly.
CI run initially failed on lint in sdk/typescript; fixed typings and re-ran CI. All checks passed on the second run and status is green.
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer: roles, stop sequences in streaming, optional streaming logprobs, function/tool-calling parity, improved streaming resume semantics. Opt-in via compat flag.
notes_for_ops: Deployment requires a config flag 'openai_compat.enabled=true' and a short rollout on Dedicated to validate perf canaries. Monitor metric compat.openai.requests.failure_rate and streaming.resume_retries.
